entries.notes: Three unobstructed stages left to right: single pot, four two-lane large beds with four separate arches, four three-level towers around a lower central biodome. Warm work lights and blue-hour valley setting; no people, text or vehicles. Middle bed count and final tower count are readable.

Three distinct connected processing stages progress from one tank and gable hall to tall multi-vessel rear plant. Repeated front gable and single leaf emblem maintain family identity. Blue-hour mountain scene, warm work lights, no people or text; scenic crates are outside the isolated-input restriction.

Three distinct warehouse stages retain closed original barn front, then broad loading arcade and final twin rear storage towers with central round dispatch crown. Consistent three-quarter front orientation. Blue-hour village setting and warm window lighting; no people or text. Each full building is inside frame.

Three distinct stages preserve two initial dispatch bays and stepped leaf parapet, increasing to wide multi-bay frontage and glazed rooftop crown. Blue-hour city hills, warm windows, clearly separated buildings, no people, lettering or vehicles.

Three separated stages retain serving window, olive awning and rounded corner. Final tall lounge has a single dominant paired botanical roof crown, conservatory and stepped terraces. Blue-hour landscape and warm windows; no people or text.

Three stages preserve recessed front porch and cream/terracotta house DNA. Mid stage adds multiple floors and curved garden bay; tall final stage shows two large solar pergolas, arcaded balconies, conservatory and triple-gable crown. No people or lettering; blue-hour setting and warm windows.

Three separated stages clearly expand from cream tank pair to tall processing factory with paired glazed rear churn towers and low central dome. Front entry and single leaf parapet preserve family identity. Blue-hour valley and warm work lighting; no people, lettering or vehicles.

Three separated stages progress from single low shop hall to twin barrel roofs and a final tall glazed atrium, curved corner and single gear crown. Consistent frontal entrance and warm cream/olive/copper architecture. Blue-hour setting, no people or text.

Three separated stages retain front oven openings, terracotta arch motif and right serving window. Mid stage has broad oven hall and solar roof; final stage adds tall triple fermentation chamber, large upper oven roof and copper chimneys. Blue-hour town setting, no people or text.

Four distinct double-deck planting units arranged 2x2, each with robust olive uprights, terracotta beds and irrigation arch. Direct comparison with T15 shows addition of the fourth unit; no count regression. Complete isolated silhouette, neutral light, no scene, people or text. Rear lower planting partly occluded by front units, expected in this three-quarter arrangement.

Exactly four separate barrel-roof greenhouse hulls in 2x2 arrangement, clearly distinct from T19 three hulls. Terracotta lower walls, olive frames and copper bands match predecessor. Two front ports clear; entire silhouette contained although side margins are narrow. No emission, text, people or loose props.

Exactly four three-chamber growing towers and a lower central biodome joined by thick pipes. Comparison with T23 confirms fourth tower plus central dome as a substantial final change. All structures and front irrigation ports visible, non-emissive green glazing, neutral studio background, no people or text.

A second full windowed processing floor now sits above the large front loading portal; comparison with T15 shows the added floor clearly. Three stepped side tanks, horizontal drum, roof solar array and rear cooling tower retained. Whole building isolated, one leaf emblem, no people, text or emission.

A triple domed vessel crown substantially changes the rear skyline versus T23 lower roofs. Front two-floor gable hall and extensive side apparatus preserved. All major structures contained, non-emissive glazing, no extra scenery or text. Dense pipe intersections still need actual 3D topology inspection.

Second front windowed storage floor is visibly added above broad loading bays compared with T15. Twin rear towers, central dispatch bridge, right closed storage wing and front round service nook preserved. Neutral isolated reference, no text or people. Thin edge vegetation approaches side frame but building is not cropped.

Twin rear towers gain recognizable gable roof crowns compared with T23 flat stepped caps. Central round dispatch volume, front loading arcade, side barrel-roofed gate and elevated right transfer bridge retained. Strong complete silhouette, one leaf emblem, neutral lighting and no people or lettering.

Damaged low two-bay urban warehouse matches opened T01 front parapet, roof tank and right service pipe. Large roof holes and wall damage differentiate ruin, with no debris field. Fully isolated, single leaf motif, no people or lettering.

Broad rear solar canopy is a clear new roof mass versus T07 bare rear roof. Three front loading bays, curved corner office and large right loading opening retained. Complete neutral-lit building, no loose props or text. Side margins are tight but no structure is cropped.

Front block gains a second full windowed floor above loading level, making three main distribution levels compared with T15 lower front block. Tall left roof tank and rear block remain. Front bay orientation unchanged, one leaf emblem, neutral isolation.

Central round roof and both linked rear towers gain pronounced sage/copper domes versus T23 low flat or rounded rectangular caps. Loading facade, rooftop curved greenhouse and right solar canopy retained. Full non-emissive studio asset, no people, text or scene.

Ruin preserves serving hatch, right entrance and olive rounded facade, with clearly broken roof, awning and windows compared with T01. Equipment remains within interior or attached to roof. Neutral isolated image, no people, text or glow.

Compact coffee serving shop with a robust shaded serving window, rounded cream/wood facade, right entrance and attached rooftop brewing vessel. Single leaf emblem, fully contained three-quarter asset, no people or text. Glazing is colored and reflective without surrounding emitted light.

Large sage-framed solar canopy supported by chunky posts newly covers front upper terrace versus T07. Serving windows and two-storey round corner preserved. Neutral isolated asset, no people, lettering or extra scene; canopy is visibly structural.

Front shop block gains a second full glazed floor above ground service, matching third sales-storey delta; T15 has only one front glazed floor. Left balcony support structure, round rear lounge and PV roof retained. Complete isolated silhouette and no unwanted lettering.

Pair of large botanical roof leaves rises above the final lounge, a distinct added skyline versus T23 low side caps. Terraces, conservatory, round lounge and three-level front shop retained. One dominant botanical crown; no second facade emblem. No people, scene or emission.

Recognizable damaged version of original cream/terracotta house: same deep porch, right recessed mailboxes, side planter and chimney. Large broken roof beams and masonry distinguish ruin without a loose rubble scene. Complete isolation, no people or text.

Small warm plaster house with deep front porch, broad entrance steps, recessed mailbox bank and integral right planter. No shop display or factory apparatus; residential identity clear. Neutral studio background and no people or lettering.

Full upper residential floor with broad window row is inserted under the existing dormer roof, versus T07 roof directly above base. Porch, side arcaded planting strip and front orientation retained. No text, people or emitted lighting.

An additional complete windowed storey beneath the dormer raises the central residential stack compared with T15; two arcaded balcony rows remain. Front porch and rounded garden bay retained. Top chimney has a tight but visible white margin; no clipping.

Rear upper housing gains three peaked sage/copper gables versus T23 low hipped roof, preserving two solar pergolas, stacked front floors, side botanical tower and glazed conservatory. Fully contained neutral-background reference. Glazing highlights are bright but show no light spill; future material QA must distinguish reflections from emission.

Ruin matches T01 cream mixing hall and paired side tanks. Major missing roof panels, tank-shell damage and masonry loss distinguish the state without a detached rubble scene. One botanical sign and clear front entry. Warm entrance fixtures and warm interior surfaces need material-lighting review.

Small cream mixing hall, exactly two attached cream side tanks, thick pipe bridge and interior vats establish butter-processing family. Whole asset is isolated. Vertical entrance fixtures appear warmly lit and interior has warm shading despite no-lit-lamps prompt; recorded separately as open visual observation.

Broad curved solar surface replaces T07 small central skylight and is a substantial upgrade. Three small side tanks, rear raised hall, large round mixing chamber, left service door and central work entry retained. Neutral background and complete silhouette. Warm entrance fixtures remain.

Added full front process floor raises hall to three main storeys versus T15 two. Curved solar roof, right manifold and three small cream tanks retained, with raised rear structures. No text or people. Warm entrance fixtures remain a material-lighting observation.

Central low drum gains a larger ribbed cream dome connected by thick pipes to two tall glazed churn vessels, forming a three-part crown compared with T23. Three-level front hall, two PV areas and right tank system retained. Glazed churn interiors clearly legible. Small entrance lamps appear illuminated; no overall dusk cast.

Ruin of broad low market retains front gear sign, supported awning, glazed shop front and roof service tank. Large roof gaps and broken boarded glazing show damage against T01. Complete isolated object, no people or text.

Low public retail hall with large shop glazing and broad front entrance/awning. Single gold gear motif; no competing botanical emblem. Cream plaster, olive fittings and reclaimed roofing follow palette, neutral lighting and complete framing.

Connected solar roofing covers both tall barrel halls versus T07 plain roofs with skylights. Same arcaded right flank, central entrance awning, side loading wing and roof machinery remain. No emission, people, text or extra scene.

An additional full glazed front sales floor raises twin barrel halls relative to side wings compared with T15. Supports and corner proportions remain clear; original entrance retained. Neutral isolated asset and one gear emblem.

Large single circular market crown bridges rear volumes above atrium versus T23 separated rear roofs; gold gear moves to crown with old front position blank, preventing duplicate emblem. Tall central greenhouse, rounded right gallery, twin barrel front roofs and service wings retained. Fully contained studio asset.

Ruin preserves large left oven mouth, right delivery hatch and tall thick chimney; missing roof surfaces and broken masonry visibly distinguish intact T01. No fire, smoke, people or loose scene. Whole asset contained.

Simple bakery identified by a single large terracotta oven mouth left and empty copper-capped serving window right. Broad timbers, cream plaster, thick chimney and one small leaf motif. Neutral isolated image; dark cold oven opening.

Large elevated blue PV canopy added over the rear baking roof compared with T07. Two front oven mouths, right delivery hatch, attached left receiving bay and side portico retained. No lit ovens, text or people. Outer side margins are narrow but complete.

A second full upper row of three closed oven arches is added above T15 first three-arch floor; two ground-level ovens and delivery hatch remain clear. PV canopy and chimney raised; right arcaded upper gallery retained. Two small functional botanical emblems are not dominant competing signs. Bright copper reflections and green sight-glass highlights show no obvious exterior light spill.

A large terracotta arch-shaped roof crown with central dark vent and lower right arch rises above T23 small upper oven room, while blue PV area and two copper chimneys remain. Original two ovens and right hatch, two full three-arch baking floors and three rear glazed kneading chambers retained. No people, lettering, smoke or glowing oven fire.

One symmetrical civic hall with broad central entrance stair, framed front botanical panel, olive/copper service forms and central mountain-and-flame crown. Crown is solid metal, not fire. No invented upgrade state. Entire asset neutral-lit and contained; no people, text or exterior scene.

One fixed civic hall faithfully uses T_FIXED massing, central entrance, botanical panel and mountain/flame crown within blue-hour Burning Hills setting. Warm windows and working lamps are appropriate for showcase. No invented three upgrade stages, no people or text. Fixed-family interpretation is explicitly distinct from upgradable showcases.

Damaged round open pavilion remains inside its intrinsic stone-bounded garden parcel, matching T01 entrances and circular benches. Broad roof gaps, split timber and broken front steps clearly distinguish ruin. No detached rubble scenery, people or text.

Single round reclaimed pavilion with broad stone benches, centered access steps, one floor mosaic and bounded integrated planting. The intrinsic garden parcel is functional park geometry, not an external scenic base. Fully contained, neutral light and no people or lettering.

Large calm round basin is visibly added at left below pergola compared with T07 paving. Two round pavilion roofs, right three-arch seating arcade, mature rear tree and central access retained. No jets or glow. Left walking loop is visually obstructed by basin/pergola; only right-hand circulation is clearly visible and actual navigability remains future 3D QA.

Original front pavilion gains a second closed upper window ring, making three total architectural levels versus T15 two. Existing rear garden hall, two rear round rooms, planted terraces, two timber pergolas, quiet basin and right stone arcade remain. One rear round roof is partially occluded by the newly raised front pavilion, as expected. Full intrinsic park boundary is within frame; no people, text, fire or glow.

A tall ribbed green-glass botanical dome replaces the low metal roof of T23 central upper garden hall, clearly changing the final skyline. Both elongated side orangery wings, paired roof-terrace trees, three-storey front pavilion (open ground plus two window rings), two open timber pergolas, right solar canopy, upper three-arch stone gallery and quiet left basin remain. The front stone arcade retains two fully visible arches and its left bay is partly hidden behind the pavilion; this single view cannot prove hidden interior clearance. Dome glazing is reflective without emitted light spill. Full intrinsic park boundary, neutral background, no people, lettering, smoke or loose scenery.

Fresh corrected ruin preserves original two-tank mixing hall, while major roof gaps, tank cracks and broken plaster establish damage. Former amber entrance lamps are absent and interior machinery is neutral gray, with no warm light spill. Complete isolated silhouette, no people or text.

Fresh corrected starter hall preserves broad central working entrance, two cream tanks, thick shared pipe bridge and single leaf sign. Entrance lamps have been removed; interior stainless machinery is dark neutral gray and has no baked amber light. No people, lettering, smoke, exterior scene or emission.

Fresh corrected T08 adds a broad blue solar barrel surface over the front mixing hall versus T07 cream roof. Three small side tanks, large left kettle, rear barrel hall and long raised process bridge retained. No visible entrance lamps or warm light spill, neutral interior machinery, complete isolated geometry.

Three clearly separated park stages left to right: T01 single open round pavilion; T12 two-storey front pavilion with two smaller rear rotundas, mature tree, quiet basin, two timber pergolas and stone seating arcade; T24 retains three-storey front pavilion and rises to central green-glass botanical dome between paired planted roof terraces and orangery wings. Right PV canopy and tiered upper stone gallery are legible. Each intrinsic park boundary remains fully visible in a shared blue-hour civic setting. Warm windows and landscape lamps are appropriate for showcase. No people, labels, text or vehicles.

Fresh corrected T16 opened directly against corrected T15. The central front now has exactly TWO full green upper window bands above the open ground processing entrance, giving three storeys; T15 had one upper band. Curved blue solar roof, one dominant leaf facade emblem, left loading bay, pair of elevated process kettles, rear-left tall vessel, rear hall, right collector above three small tanks and separate rear-right buffer remain readable. Rear bridge details are more occluded behind the taller front and cannot be fully certified from this angle. Door-side amber lamps are absent; gold impact bollards remain unlit, interior vessels are neutral gray and green windows show no visible halo or warm facade light spill. Complete isolated subject on white, narrow uncut margins, no people, text or vehicles. Prior lighting defect is resolved in this required sample.

Fresh corrected T24 opened directly against corrected T23. A substantial tall opaque cream central upper kettle with brass equator and rounded dome replaces the low-lid silhouette, retaining a readable lower round base. Two large sage/brass upper arches connect this new central volume to the two separately visible dark green glass mixing towers. Their domes, gray internal paddles, terrace and right stair persist. Both solar areas, central front ground entrance plus exactly two upper green window rows, left loading bay, hygiene tower, partly occluded left opaque mixers, horizontal right collector, three small right tanks and large separate rear-right buffer remain readable. Dark green glazing has no halo; gray interior machinery and unlit gold impact bollards show no amber entrance strips or warm facade light spill. Complete isolated asset with very narrow but uncut lower/lateral margins; full highest pipe and foundation corners inside frame. No people, text, vehicles or loose props. Prior lighting defect is resolved in this required sample. Hidden rear interfaces and actual supporting geometry still require later mesh QA.

Replacement wide showcase freshly opened together with corrected T01/T12/T24 references. Three complete separate stages read clearly left to right. T01 retains patchwork gable, two side tanks, top pipe and open front machinery bay. T12 retains one full upper front window row, curved blue solar hood, left loading wing, paired elevated opaque process kettles, long rear bridge, three small right tanks and a distinct separate large rear-right buffer. T24 retains exactly two upper front window rows above the ground entrance, both solar areas, terrace/right stair, three small right tanks plus separate large buffer, and all three crown vessels: paired dark glass mixing towers with visible paddles flanking the new opaque cream central kettle and two upper connecting arches. Building identities and progressive massing are readable without crop or overlap. Warm interior and exterior lighting belongs to this intended blue-hour landscape showcase; it is not reused as a neutral mesh input. No people, readable text or vehicles. The updated showcase closes the withdrawn original reference-chain issue. Distant scenery is illustrative, not an additional production building asset.

review_method: Every listed full PNG and listed predecessor was opened separately using view_image; notes describe visual observation. Hashes bind exact viewed files; reopened butter files resolve to their explicit archived source.
limitations: This is a raster-art review, not mesh, material, collider, performance or Unity Game View acceptance.
Occluded rear geometry and actual +Z orientation/pivot require later 3D inspection.
Narrow but uncut margins are documented; literal 10-12 percent prompt margins were not achieved by every render.

Original butter inputs contained warm lit fixtures. They were withdrawn and archived; all five replacement mandatory samples and the replacement showcase passed fresh independent agent review. Historical correction records are retained, not counted as current passing images.

findings.detail: Small vertical amber entry lamps and warm interior material appear illuminated; T24 also shows local warm facade light spill. Contradicts neutral input/no-lit-lamp prompt. Original accepted chain is being archived and replaced; original showcase itself permits lighting but must follow updated image provenance.
findings.resolution: All five corrected butter mandatory inputs were independently reopened and passed against current accepted hashes; the replacement showcase was independently compared with corrected T01/T12/T24 and passed. Original defective image observations remain bound to unchanged explicit archives.

original_preservation.explanation: Mobile_RPAsset.asset differs from the initial session baseline. It already differed in the captured snapshot before the exclusively owned Unity acceptance run; this audit does not attribute its earlier change or revert it.

limits: This audit read existing Unity results and checked their source/artifact hashes. It did not launch Unity or rerun tests.

The technical snapshot above records the earlier incomplete-art Unity intake. A final read-only Unity validation is coordinated separately by root and the Unity agent; this completed art review does not close that gate.
No FBX models are assigned; actual model topology/material/collider/runtime QA is a later user workflow.

showcase_comparison_reference_reviews.notes: Corrected showcase middle-stage reference opened independently with T11 predecessor: one full green upper window band has been added above the open ground processing doorway; neutral gray metal equipment inside, gold door bollards without visible emission. Curved blue solar roof, two left tall process kettles, elevated rear bridge, three small right tanks and separate large rear-right buffer are retained. Complete isolated building with narrow but uncut lateral margins. No text, people, vehicles or warm facade light spill. This reference read supports the later corrected showcase comparison, not an acceptance record mutation.

not_closed_by_this_report: Actual 3D mesh, material, pivot, collider, navigation and performance acceptance; Meshy remains a separate manual user workflow.
The final Unity intake result after all 251 reference images exists is reported separately by the Unity agent and merged by root.

final_art_qa_summary.scope_note: Combined scope is 50 required tier samples, the fixed town hall reference, and 11 family showcases. Prior independently reviewed unchanged images are reused by exact hash; this agent did not claim to reopen every inherited image. Extra cultivation T20 and separately documented corrected butter T12 support targeted comparisons. This is agent visual review, not a personal human approval.
